_schema.purpose: Single source of truth for what Pulse may auto-fix. One record per action-template. Check 0 (durable triage, PR B) reads this to decide auto-fix vs ask; Check V (promotion loop, PR C) reads/writes clean_streak + state to graduate/demote. See docs/pulse-triage-layer-brief.md.

record_shape.template: kebab-case id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ — the stable prefix of an intervention_id '<template>:<detail>'. Must equal cycle_prime_ledger.canonical_intervention_id()'s template.
record_shape.state: 'probation' (ask-first; building track record) | 'graduated' (auto-fix eligible). Only Check V flips probation->graduated, and only after Larry approval.
record_shape.reversible: bool. Only reversible templates may ever graduate.
record_shape.permanent_guard: bool. Credential / money / irreversible-or-destructive. A permanent_guard template ALWAYS asks and can NEVER graduate, regardless of track record.
record_shape.clean_streak: int. Consecutive clean executions (reversible, zero Larry-corrections). Reset to 0 on any miss/correction.
record_shape.total_dispatches: int. Lifetime dispatch count for this template (audit only; not a graduation gate).
record_shape.last_larry_correction_at: iso8601 utc | null. Stamped on demotion.
record_shape.graduated_at: iso8601 utc | null. Stamped when Larry approves graduation.

plain_language.what: Plain-English description of the signal this template responds to.
plain_language.action: Plain-English description of what Pulse does automatically once graduated.

_schema.graduate_requires: state=probation AND reversible AND permanent_guard=false AND clean_streak>=graduate_min_clean_streak AND Larry approval. Check V (PR C) enforces this; it unifies the legacy pulse_check_v GRADUATE_MIN_DISPATCHES (>=10) down to this value.
_schema.track_record_source: clean_streak is a DERIVED CACHE reconciled by Check V from the authoritative executions store at ~/agents/state/action-template-executions.json ({action_templates: {<template>: {executions: [{outcome, larry_correction_signal, ts}]}}}). Written by alert_triage_state.record_action_template_execution() (Check 0, for Tier-1 auto-fixes AND Tier-2 approved-probation fixes); single reader = pulse_check_v.consecutive_clean_streak() (consecutive success+uncorrected from the tail). The streak is NEVER read from cycle-prime-ledger payload.larry_modified.
_schema.guard_list_relationship: This registry SUPERSEDES a standalone config/action-template-guard-list.json (which does not exist on disk). The guarded set is a DERIVED VIEW computed at read time: { r.template for r in patterns if r.state != 'graduated' or r.permanent_guard }. PR C wires Check V to derive the guarded set from this rule; no separate guard-list file is created. See docs/pulse-triage-layer-brief.md.
_schema.demotion_rule: Automatic, no approval: on any failed execution OR Larry-correction of a graduated template, flip state->probation, reset clean_streak=0, stamp last_larry_correction_at. Trust is lost faster than earned.
_schema.seeding_note: Seeded 2026-06-03 (PR A). Routine reversible self-heal templates start in probation (they earn auto-fix via track record). Credential/money/irreversible templates start permanent_guard=true and never graduate.

plain_language.what: A reserved 'classify me' bucket — NOT a real action template. The ledger normalizes any intervention/systemic-fix recorded without a --template into 'uncategorized:<detail>' so the data point is preserved and visible instead of being dropped as an empty-id row.
plain_language.action: Never auto-fix. Someone reviews the row, identifies the real action class, and re-tags the action under its proper template. This bucket exists only so untagged interventions stay countable until classified.
plain_language.why_safe: It performs no action at all; it is a placeholder. It is permanent_guard=true and reversible=false purely so it can NEVER graduate to auto-fix — a classify-me bucket must always ask, by definition.

plain_language.what: A systemd unit shipped in the repo drifts out of install (present in systemd/ but missing from /etc/systemd/system/).
plain_language.action: Re-install the unit (cp + daemon-reload + enable --now) and confirm it is running.
plain_language.why_safe: It's a reversible re-install from the repo's own source-of-truth; it restores the intended state and changes nothing else.

plain_language.what: A managed daemon (a healer, shipper, or bot service) has stalled or is running stale code after a merge.
plain_language.action: Restart the systemd service and confirm the heartbeat / liveness check recovers.
plain_language.why_safe: A restart is reversible and idempotent; the service comes back on the same config, and a failed restart surfaces immediately.

plain_language.what: ourliberty-sync's push to origin/main failed on a transient (rejected fast-forward that a rebase resolves).
plain_language.action: Rebase onto origin/main and retry the push once.
plain_language.why_safe: It's a rebase-and-retry of an already-committed change; a real divergence still fails loudly rather than forcing anything.

plain_language.what: A credential / OAuth token / API key needs rotation or re-authentication.
plain_language.action: ASK Larry — never auto-rotate. Credentials are a permanent_guard floor.
plain_language.why_safe: Rotation can lock out a live account and is not cleanly reversible; it always requires a human.

plain_language.what: An alert implies a money movement (refund, charge, payout adjustment).
plain_language.action: ASK Larry — never move money automatically. Money is a permanent_guard floor.
plain_language.why_safe: Money movements are not reversible without cost and always require a human.

plain_language.what: An alert implies a destructive or irreversible action (deleting data/branches, force-push to main, dropping state).
plain_language.action: ASK Larry — never auto-execute destructive actions. Irreversible actions are a permanent_guard floor.
plain_language.why_safe: By definition there is no clean undo; a human must decide.
